title: Thunderbird automatically marks new emails as read
creator: ag.ageseta
content:
Hello,

I am having an issue with Thunderbird automatically marking new emails as read.

When a new email arrives, it initially appears as unread in Thunderbird, but after a short time it automatically changes to read, even though I have not opened or clicked on the email.

I use Thunderbird on two computers – a desktop computer at the office and a laptop when working from home. The problem started after I installed and configured Thunderbird with the same email account on my laptop.

I have already disabled the “Automatically mark messages as read” option in Thunderbird. I have also repaired/reindexed the Inbox folder, but the problem remains.

The email account is configured using IMAP on the laptop.

An important detail: when I check the same emails in Gmail through a web browser, they are still marked as Unread. Only Thunderbird shows them as Read.

Could using the same email account in Thunderbird on two different computers be causing this issue? Could there be a synchronization or local Thunderbird setting that changes the read/unread status?

Could you please advise what I should check or change to fix this?

Thank you.

title: Thunderbird authentication issue with secondary Outlook account
creator: erdemonal11
content:
Hello,

I'm having an authentication issue with Thunderbird on Fedora when trying to add a second Microsoft account.

My main @outlook.com account works without any problems using IMAP/SMTP and OAuth2. However, I can't get my @outlook.fr account to work.

For the @outlook.fr account, I'm using:

IMAP: outlook.office365.com, port 993, SSL/TLS, OAuth2 SMTP: smtp.office365.com, port 587, STARTTLS, OAuth2

When I add the account, the Microsoft login page opens normally. I sign in with the @outlook.fr account, complete 2FA, and Microsoft confirms that the account has been successfully connected to Thunderbird.

However, as soon as I return to Thunderbird, I get an authentication error saying that it was unable to log in to outlook.office365.com with that username.

I've already tried clearing Thunderbird's saved passwords, cookies, and web cache. I also confirmed that IMAP is enabled in Outlook web settings, checked the account aliases/sign-in preferences, and verified the server names and ports.

Since the Microsoft authentication itself completes successfully, I'm not sure why Thunderbird fails immediately afterwards. The same setup works with my @outlook.com account, so the problem seems to be specific to the second account.

Has anyone encountered this before, or is there anything else I should check?

Thanks.
